answer.evidence: The car body is drawn as one tall stack of horizontal surfaces: trunk (rows 1-9), rear glass (10-14), roof (15-29), windshield (30-35) and hood (36-46). The hood ends in a light front-edge line at row 45 (#8ca29d), followed by darker shadow rows 46-47. Below that is a vertical front face of about 15 rows (rows 47-62) holding the grille with dark slats, headlights and bumper. The top is drawn very tall and close to plan view, but it does end in a front-edge line and eave shadow above a front face of more than 3 rows. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts put the candidate level with the richer references. It has 17 visible tones per tile, matching prop-stall-cheese (17) and just under prop-well-roofed (20). Near-flat coverage is 7%, below the cheese stall's 13%. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted, a dark teal or green-brown beside the body panels rather than black. By eye, the body panels have a few lightness steps (highlight, mid, dark, deep). Rust patches, cracked-glass lines, the grille and the bumper break up the surface, and the windshield and roof panels are separated by value rather than a uniform line. Texture is somewhat less dense than the best references, since the roof and hood panels are smooth in places, but there are no large flat fills. It would sit acceptably beside the references.
